notes: Frozen regression set for /prospect. Headless cases: records are given, tools are unavailable. Covers the traps found in the 17 Sep 2026 live Exa test (stale signal, CTO not CEO, email at a previous employer) plus suppression, ICP rejection, no-email and selective send.

cases.input: Today is 2026-09-17. Headless test: tools are not available, so decide and write using only the records given. Prospect record: Tidewater Labs (tidewaterlabs.com.au), Perth, B2B software, 24 staff, founder-led. Signals: $4M seed announced 2026-09-01 (StartupDaily); Head of Growth role posted on Seek 2026-09-08. Decision maker: Priya Raman, Co-founder and CEO. Email lookup: priya@tidewaterlabs.com.au. Not in suppression, no Gmail history. Score it, then write the draft email exactly as it would go into Gmail (Subject line, body, sign-off).

expects.assertion: The score is at least 5 and the decision is to draft.
The opening uses the funding and the Head of Growth role together as one argument about what the money is for, rather than listing two facts.
Exactly one sentence describes Corient as an embedded CMO with a pod of specialists or a marketing team for the cost of one hire, it is near the end, and it does not read as a pitch or list services.
The body ends with exactly one curious question about their plan and does not ask for a call or meeting.
The body, excluding the sign-off, is 80 words or fewer.
Nothing asserts a fact about the prospect's internal spend, stack, team skills or results.

cases.input: Today is 2026-09-17. Headless test: tools are not available, so decide and write using only the records given. Prospect record: Loam & Co (loamandco.com), Melbourne, premium skincare, 30 staff, founder-led, about $6M revenue. Signal: Performance Marketing Manager role posted 2026-09-10 on LinkedIn Jobs. Decision maker: Jess Tran, Founder. Email lookup: jess@loamandco.com. No suppression hit, no Gmail history. Score it and write the draft email if it qualifies.

expects.assertion: Scores 5 (marketing hire 4, founder +1) and writes a draft email.
The offer sentence ties the marketing team for the cost of one hire to the role they are hiring for.
